name: Extended Surface Derivatives
definition: A method that extends surface optimization by introducing non-local perturbations to a surface $\tilde{S}$. It tests how potential surfaces could exist at sampled positions as perturbations to $\tilde{S}$, effectively exploring an extended parameter space $S$ to refine $\tilde{S}$.
summary: Extended Surface Derivatives optimize surfaces by unifying shading and boundary derivatives into a single non-local term, enabling access to concave regions otherwise inaccessible.
